hook: Four buildings of the Southern Pacific hospital block: powerhouse, paint shop, nurses' annex and Huntington Social Hall.

historical_record.description: The four-storey annex housing the hospital's nurses was built first, before the hospital itself — rusticated brick over a high concrete foundation on the lower two storeys, smooth brick with corner quoins above, under a moulded sheet-metal dentil cornice. A drug room stood at its east end and a laundry in the basement.

The powerhouse was built at the high northwest corner of the block, one tall storey over a basement in rusticated painted brick under a sheet-metal cornice and stucco parapet, with a stuccoed stack rising about thirty feet and a steel extension above it. It held two 75-kilowatt generators and two boilers, and basement tunnels ran from it to a coal and oil vault under the Lyon Street pavement and across to the annex.

Huntington Social Hall was built for the patients' recreation, two storeys measuring 35 by 65 feet, with a central portico on paired Tuscan columns and its name cut in Roman letters along the cornice. It was the joint gift of Collis P. Huntington's widow and his nephew H. E. Huntington, as a memorial to him. Two tiled social rooms flanked the ground-floor hall, with eight bedrooms above.
A small single-storey storage and paint shop was put up just west of the annex, a frame building faced in brick veneer with its rusticated courses lined up with the annex's.
The balustrade above the annex cornice came down and a new coping was built in its place.

Huntington Social Hall was partitioned into administrative offices on both floors; some of those partitions came out again under a 1966 permit, by which time it was called the Huntington Office Annex.

The annex was gutted and rebuilt to hold 45 patient rooms under the architect Elmer Botsai, the first stage of a seven-year rebuilding programme. The central stair came out for a lift, the ornamental wrought iron fire escapes at each end were replaced with large exterior stairs, and the windows beside them were bricked up.

Listed on the National Register of Historic Places with the hospital building to the south as the Southern Pacific Company Hospital Historic District: the flagship of the first hospital system in the world built by a company for its own employees, and an intact piece of early twentieth-century institutional architecture.

building.architect_note: Patterson designed the annex and the powerhouse; the architect of Huntington Social Hall is not established.
building.completed_conflict: The assessor gives 1908 for the parcel, which carries four buildings finished in 1907, 1908, 1911 and about 1923.
